title: MFA confirms advance voting for Thais in Cambodia is secured despite tensions

summary: Defense Minister Gen. Natthaphon Narkphanit announced that Thai military forces will remain deployed along the Cambodian border for at least one year to safeguard sovereignty. The ministry plans to install electronic fencing, CCTV systems, and permanent physical barriers in key areas to maintain control.
title: Troops to man border for 'at least one year'

summary: The 2nd Army Region issued a statement today declaring the border situation is still not completely safe. Officials asked the public to follow military instructions strictly to ensure civilian safety and maintain the secrecy of military positions during this period of high alert.
title: Army Region 2 warns situation still unsafe at Thailand-Cambodia border

summary: Army Chief Gen. Pana Klaewplodtook visited the Suranaree Force in Surin province today to monitor the security situation. He emphasized the importance of maintaining strong defensive lines and monitoring the welfare of frontline troops stationed along the border with Cambodia.
title: Thai Army Chief inspects Surin border units under Suranaree Force

summary: Associate Professor Chidtawan Chanakul has called on all political parties contesting the upcoming 2026 election to state whether they will open or keep closed the border checkpoints. The debate centers on balancing economic trade needs with national security and the ongoing territorial dispute.
title: Academic urges political parties to clarify position on Thai-Cambodian border crossings

summary: The United States has allocated $15 million to assist displaced families and $10 million for demining efforts along the border. US official Michael DeSombre expressed hope for lasting peace following the July and October agreements involving regional leaders.
title: US Pledges to Keep An Eye on Border Situation Amid Ceasefire

summary: Troops from the 29th Infantry Regiment visited Aranyaprathet, Sa Kaeo, to distribute winter blankets to the elderly and gifts to local students. The mission aims to provide mental rehabilitation and strengthen military-civilian ties following the recent border conflict.
title: ทหารราบ29 เติมสุข บุกชายแดน 'ไทย-กัมพูชา' มอบผ้าห่ม-ของขวัญ วันเด็ก
titleEn: 29th Infantry Regiment delivers blankets and Children's Day gifts to Thai-Cambodian border communities

summary: Army Chief Gen. Pana Klaewplodtook visited strategic border outposts in Surin province, including Hill 225, Hill 350, and Ta Kwai Sanctuary. He emphasized the importance of maintaining strong defensive lines and instructed units to adapt their deployment strategies to suit the terrain for maximum security.
title: ผบ.ทบ.ลุยตรวจแนวชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา 'เนิน 225-350-ปราสาทตาควาย'
titleEn: Army Chief inspects Thai-Cambodian border at 'Hill 225, Hill 350, and Ta Kwai Sanctuary'

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has backed the revision of MoUs 43 and 44 with Cambodia. He argued that land border demarcation should utilize modern technology like LiDAR to resolve complex areas. While his caretaker government lacks the mandate for binding changes, he stressed the need for a framework that uses internationally recognized standards to prevent future disputes.
title: PM calls for border MoU updates, suggests LiDAR technology for demarcation

summary: Thai Caretaker PM Anutin Charnvirakul suggested that MoUs 43 and 44 signed in 2000 and 2001 should be revised or replaced using modern technology. He noted his caretaker government cannot make binding changes but emphasized the need for stability before elections.
title: Thai PM calls for overhaul of border MoUs with Cambodia amid poll campaign tensions

summary: Reporters from Cambodia describe their experiences covering the 21-day conflict in provinces like Oddar Meanchey and Banteay Meanchey. The reporting focused on civilian evacuations and the destruction of homes, monasteries, and schools caused by heavy artillery and aerial bombing during the peak of the fighting.
title: Journalism on the front line: Cambodian reporters risk lives to document war and counter disinformation

summary: PM Hun Manet outlined a recovery plan focusing on the return of displaced residents and clearing unexploded ordnance. US Assistant Secretary Michael DeSombre met with Cambodian officials to urge full compliance with the ceasefire and announced the release of 18 captured Cambodian soldiers.
title: Cambodia identifies priority measures to address impacts of border tensions

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that the border situation has improved following the December 27 ceasefire and the release of 18 captive soldiers. He announced infrastructure reconstruction plans for roads and schools and thanked China for providing emergency humanitarian aid shipments to displaced civilians.
title: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet announces measures to address impacts of the border conflict, thanks China's support

summary: As of January 8, 2026, over 173,000 people remain displaced in Cambodia following the border conflict that peaked in late December. While 71% of the initial 649,000 displaced persons have returned home, many cannot return due to landmine contamination (UXOs) and damaged infrastructure. Areas like Siem Reap and Banteay Meanchey host the largest remaining displaced populations.
title: World Vision Situation Report: Displacement Caused by Cambodia-Thailand Border Conflict

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported a 'fragile' situation despite the Dec 27 ceasefire. A Jan 6 firing incident in Ubon Ratchathani injured one Thai soldier; Cambodia later expressed regret, claiming it was an accidental explosion during cleaning activities. Thailand formally protested what it calls 'unfounded accusations' regarding territorial annexation and interference in Thai domestic politics.
title: Summary of the Weekly Press Briefing on Thai-Cambodian Border Situation

summary: Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs highlighted a specific breach of the December 27 ceasefire on January 6, 2026, when projectiles from Cambodia reportedly injured Thai soldiers. Bangkok is urging Phnom Penh to return to peaceful negotiations and stop actions that undermine trust.
title: Thai MFA Demands Cambodia Halt ‘Provocations’ and Election Interference

summary: International reporting highlights the rising tension as Cambodia claims Thai forces remain in four border locations despite the December 27 truce. The report notes that the conflict, which stems from century-old territorial disputes, has seen a recent surge in military activity including fighter jets and rocket fire. While a ceasefire is officially in place, the 'war of words' over territorial occupation continues to prevent displaced civilians from returning to their villages.
title: Cambodia says Thai troops continue to 'occupy' civilian areas, testing December truce

summary: Cambodia has officially stated it will not recognize any border alterations resulting from the use of force. Government spokesperson Pen Bona accused Thailand of delaying a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting originally set for early January in Siem Reap. Cambodia alleges Thai forces are 'illegally occupying' territory in Oddar Meanchey, Preah Vihear, Banteay Meanchey, and Pursat. Despite this, approximately 490,000 of the 640,000 displaced persons have returned home since the December 26 ceasefire.
title: Cambodia rejects redrawing of border by Thai military

summary: While nationalist sentiment is high on social media, anti-war movements in both Thailand and Cambodia are gaining visibility. In Chiang Mai, students and residents protested against the armed clashes, emphasizing that citizens on both sides want peace and stability. The article warns that online propaganda is fueling hostility while real lives at the border are being disrupted, with children forced into shelters.
title: Thais and Cambodians speak out against the looming war

summary: A verified investigation by Nikkei Asia has identified at least 110 Cambodian security personnel killed during the 21 days of intense border fighting in December. While the Cambodian government has not released an official national death toll, the names were verified through official social media condolences and funeral notices from high-ranking officials. Some estimates suggest the toll could exceed 130.
title: Nikkei Asia: Cambodian soldier death toll in border conflict exceeds 110

summary: This analysis discusses the December 27 ceasefire agreement, which uniquely included a clause for both sides to refrain from spreading fake news. It highlights that narrative warfare on social media continues to fuel nationalism even while kinetic operations have largely paused. It mentions mediation efforts by Malaysia, the US, and ASEAN.
title: Cambodia-Thailand Border Conflict: Restraint in the Digital Information Battlefield

summary: The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) conducted six monitoring missions along the Thailand-Cambodia border in the first half of January to maintain peace. Cambodia reaffirmed its commitment to a mine-free world and peaceful dialogue regarding border disputes.
title: Top News Headlines In Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore & Vietnam: Jan 14, 2026

summary: Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn accused Thai forces of continuing to occupy civilian areas inside Cambodian territory despite the December ceasefire. He alleged that Thai troops have set up barbed wire and containers in frontier zones, preventing approximately 4,000 families from returning home. While the ceasefire has largely held, Phnom Penh warns that these unresolved deployments threaten the fragile peace. Thai officials have dismissed the claims as 'baseless,' stating their positions are consistent with agreed de-escalation measures.
title: Cambodia Says Thai Troops Still Hold Civilian Areas, Putting Border Truce at Risk

summary: Cambodia reported on Wednesday that Thailand has requested to postpone a special meeting of the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) for the second time. The meeting, originally proposed for mid-January in Siem Reap, was delayed by the Thai side due to internal procedures and the need to appoint a new JBC composition following the upcoming February general election. In response, Cambodia has requested that Joint Survey Teams be dispatched between January 19 and 30 to continue boundary marking while waiting for the official meeting.
title: Cambodia says Thailand requests to postpone special meeting on border demarcation for 2nd time

summary: Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn told Reuters that Thai troops are still occupying territories inside Cambodia, using barbed wire and containers to block areas. He stated 4,000 families cannot return home. Thailand's Foreign Ministry dismissed these claims as baseless, stating troop positions comply with de-escalation agreements.
title: Cambodia says Thai troops still occupy civilian areas, testing December truce

summary: Reports highlight a growing risk to the December ceasefire as Cambodia identifies four specific border locations of alleged Thai incursions. The report mentions previous Chinese-led mediation in Yunnan and a significant displacement of civilians following 20 days of heavy fighting in December 2025.
title: Fears over fragile truce as Cambodia says Thailand is still occupying civilian areas

summary: Tensions are escalating as Cambodia identifies at least four locations where it claims Thai military units are stationed deep inside its territory. The report highlights that the December fighting killed 101 people and displaced over 500,000. While the ceasefire has largely held, the unresolved troop deployments are viewed by Phnom Penh as a violation of the spirit of the truce.
title: Border Tensions Rise As Cambodia Says Thai Military Occupies Territory

summary: Thailand has requested a second postponement of the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting originally planned for January in Siem Reap. The Thai side cited internal procedures and the need to appoint a new commission following the formation of a new Cabinet after the early February General Election. Cambodia has expressed a desire to resume joint survey work and the placement of temporary markers despite the delay.
title: Thai Political Transition Stalls Border Peace as JBC Meeting Postponed for Second Time

summary: The Cambodian State Secretariat of Border Affairs reported that Thailand requested to postpone a special Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting originally proposed for mid-January in Siem Reap. The delay is attributed to Thailand's internal procedures for appointing a new commission following the general election scheduled for February 8, 2026. In response, Cambodia has urged the dispatch of Joint Survey Teams to resume technical work and place temporary markers between January 19 and 30.
title: Cambodia says Thailand requests to postpone border meeting for 2nd time

summary: The December 27 truce is facing significant stress as Cambodia prioritizes the issue of 'occupied villages' in its diplomatic agenda. While fighting has ceased, Thai officials indicate that no significant changes to border demarcation or troop withdrawals will occur until a new Thai government is formed following the February 8 general election. China has been noted as an 'active contributor' to the recent diplomatic efforts to maintain the ceasefire.
title: Thai troop presence in civilian areas threatens cross-border ceasefire

summary: Following the border ceasefire, the two nations are looking to resume talks on the 26,000-square-kilometer Overlapping Claims Area (OCA) in the Gulf of Thailand. Thai PM Paetongtarn Shinawatra has informed her Cambodian counterpart of the intent to reactivate the Joint Technical Committee (JTC) to discuss joint energy development.
title: Thailand, Cambodia to resume negotiations on sea disputes

summary: Military officials from both nations met at the Choam-Sa Ngam border crossing on January 15 to discuss strengthening the December 27 ceasefire terms. The talks focused on implementing the joint outcomes of the General Border Committee (GBC) to maintain peace and prevent fresh provocations along the frontier.
title: Thailand, Cambodia hold talks to ensure ceasefire

summary: Analytic report detailing how Thailand targeted six casino and hotel complexes (including O'Smach Resort) during December clashes, alleging they served as military-backed scam centers. The strikes caused civilian casualties and the flight of thousands of trafficked victims held in these compounds.
title: From Fraud to the Frontlines: Scam Centers Caught in the Cambodia-Thailand Conflict

summary: Military officials from Cambodia and Thailand met Thursday morning at the Choam-Sa Ngam International Point of Entry to discuss strengthening the Dec. 27 ceasefire. The meeting focused on implementing joint statements from the General Border Committee (GBC) to seek a 'peaceful, just, and lasting solution' following the three-week conflict in December.
title: Cambodia-Thailand Regional Border Committee secretariat officials meet to enforce ceasefire

summary: Senior military officials from Thailand's Second Army Area and Cambodia's Military Region 4 met on Thursday at the Chong Sa-ngam border checkpoint. The Regional Border Committee (RBC) meeting focused on strengthening coordination, appointing liaison officers for faster communication, and addressing measures to prevent accidents among troops. They also discussed cooperation on clearing landmines in inland areas to improve safety for local communities.
title: Military officers meet at the border

summary: The United States announced $45 million in aid to support Thailand and Cambodia following the October 2025 Kuala Lumpur Peace Accords. The funding is intended to promote regional stability, address the ongoing danger of land mines, and support the implementation of the ceasefire after months of clashes that killed dozens.
title: U.S. aid to help ensure stability, prosperity at Cambodia-Thailand border

summary: Reporting from O'Smach reveals rows of idle construction cranes and unexploded ordnance in civilian courtyards. Thailand defends its December air strikes as a 'war against the Scam Army,' alleging these compounds housed kamikaze drones and military equipment. Residents remain nervous, citing rumors of snipers and looting despite the Dec 27 ceasefire.
title: Fear, suspicion, and destroyed scam compounds at Cambodian border town weeks after Thai air strikes

summary: Cambodia has lodged a formal protest following the Royal Thai Navy's seizure of a fishing boat on January 6 near Koh Kong province. While the four crew members were released on January 11, Cambodia demands the immediate return of the vessel, asserting it was in Cambodian waters. Thailand maintains the boat was in Thai territory without registration.
title: Cambodia protests Thai navy seizure of fishing boat

summary: The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) inspected civilian infrastructure in Pursat province that was damaged by Thai military artillery and airstrikes. Governor Khoy Rida led the delegation to verify the impact on local communities following the December 2025 de-escalation agreements.
title: VIDEO: ASEAN Team inspects civilian damage in Cambodia's border provinces

summary: Thailand's Joint Information Center on the Thailand-Cambodia Situation issued a statement rejecting a report titled “Thailand–Cambodia Conflict: Incursions, IHL Violations, and Scam Networks.” The military claims the document is biased, lacks independent verification, and ignores Cambodian use of landmines and force against Thai soldiers.
title: Army rejects Cambodia-linked report as one-sided, misleading

summary: As of January 15, 2026, over 141,850 people remain displaced due to the border conflict. While some essential services have resumed, many families are unable to return due to housing damage and ongoing safety concerns. Humanitarian agencies continue to provide aid across provinces including Banteay Meanchey and Preah Vihear, targeting vulnerable groups like children and pregnant women.
title: World Vision Situation Report #22: Displacement Caused by Cambodia -Thailand Border Conflict

summary: Pursat Governor Khoy Rida told the ASEAN Observation Team (AOT) that Thai troops are maintaining an 'invasion and occupation' of four locations within Cambodian territory, specifically near the Thmor Da area. He reported that over 80 families have been directly impacted, with many unable to return to their homes due to Thai razor-wire fences and military presence.
title: Pursat Governor: Thai troops occupying Cambodian territory more than a 'border clash'

summary: Rights group LICADHO reported on Tuesday that Thai forces demolished a 'significant number' of Cambodian homes and structures in contested border areas of Banteay Meanchey province. The group cited satellite imagery showing clearing activities after the December 27 ceasefire. Thailand's foreign ministry previously rejected allegations of annexation, stating security measures are in compliance with the truce. Over 127,000 Cambodians remain in displacement camps.
title: Thai forces razed Cambodian homes on border: Rights group

summary: Cambodia has lodged a formal diplomatic protest against Thailand over military construction activities on January 19 at three border locations. Allegations include the installation of a Buddha statue in the An Ses area (Preah Vihear) and the construction of bunkers using heavy machinery in Banteay Meanchey. Phnom Penh claims these actions violate the recent ceasefire and sovereign integrity.
title: Cambodia Protests Thai Installations and Construction at Three Border Locations

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal protest against the Thai armed forces for activities in areas it describes as occupied Cambodian territory. Specifically, Phnom Penh cited the reinstallation of razor wire at the Thmar Da International Point of Entry on January 16 as a violation of sovereignty that undermines the de-escalation efforts agreed upon in the December 27 Joint Statement.
title: Cambodia protests Thai military actions on border

summary: The South Korean government has pledged $500,000 in funding through UNICEF to address the humanitarian crisis caused by the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict. The aid is intended to support the estimated 500,000 people displaced by the fighting that escalated in late 2025. This follows international efforts to clear landmines and facilitate the return of civilians after the early December ceasefire.
title: S. Korea To Provide Humanitarian Aid For Thai-Cambodian Border Dispute

summary: Thailand will enshrine the ashes of four soldiers killed during the December 2025 border clashes at the Victory Monument on February 3. The Thai military reports that while the situation has largely de-escalated, tensions remain as they monitor Cambodian troop movements and repairs. Meanwhile, an ASEAN Observers Team and foreign military attachés have been briefed on the second wave of conflict in Si Sa Ket and Ubon Ratchathani.
title: Ashes of fallen troops bound for Victory Monument

summary: Thailand has utilized formal diplomatic channels to address an open letter written by a Cambodian senator that referenced the Thai monarchy. Thai officials described the letter as 'highly inappropriate' and an interference in internal affairs. The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs emphasized managing the issue quietly to maintain stability and adhere to ASEAN diplomatic norms.
title: Thailand responds to controversial Cambodian letter through diplomatic channels

summary: Thai authorities confirmed a Buddha statue was erected at the disputed border site known as An Ma (Thailand) or An Ses (Cambodia). This follows the destruction of a Hindu deity (Vishnu) statue by Thai forces in December, which had caused diplomatic friction. The area remains a flashpoint despite the December 27 ceasefire agreement.
title: Buddha statue built in place of Hindu one on disputed Thai-Cambodian border

summary: According to reports from the Cambodian Interior Ministry, approximately 82% of the 640,000 people displaced by recent border fighting have returned home. Around 116,779 people remain in displacement camps. Additionally, Russia has provided its third round of humanitarian aid, including household items, to the Cambodian Red Cross to assist affected families.
title: Majority of displaced people return home following Thailand-Cambodia ceasefire

summary: The upcoming Thai election is identified as the single biggest factor for the future of border relations. The report highlights that relations fell to a decade-low in 2025 due to armed conflict involving airpower. A victory for the Prachachon Party could shift relations toward institution-based diplomacy, while a conservative win might see the border issue continue as a nationalist tool. Trade losses currently exceed $4.7 billion annually due to gate closures.
title: The Possibility of Restoring Cambodia-Thailand Relations After the Thai General Election on February 8, 2026

summary: Approximately 530,000 of the 640,000 Cambodians displaced by the border conflict have returned home. However, 116,779 people remain in displacement camps. While public services like schools and hospitals are gradually reopening in provinces like Oddar Meanchey and Preah Vihear, some remain closed due to security concerns. Cambodia continues to warn that certain Thai military actions undermine de-escalation efforts.
title: 82% of displaced Cambodians return home as ceasefire holds

summary: Thai Supreme Commander Gen Ukrit emphasizes that while the situation has stabilized following the ceasefire, both sides are installing defensive barriers. He urged caution regarding 'peace feelers' and noted that Thailand is preparing for all scenarios across diplomacy, military, and economic fronts.
title: Thai supreme commander urges caution on Cambodia 'peace feeler' claims

summary: Thai Prime Minister and Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul visited Sa Kaeo province on January 26 to assess the border. He stated that both militaries are in communication and adhering to the December 27, 2025 agreement. Regarding reports of Cambodia digging tactical trenches, Anutin noted that each country has the right to defend its territory. He also addressed humanitarian mine clearance as a binding global obligation.
title: Thai-Cambodian Border Remains Stable Anutin Confident No Third Round of Clashes

summary: Analysis suggests the 2025 conflict was driven by Thailand's crackdown on border scam centers and plans to legalize casinos, which threatened Cambodian elite revenue streams, leading to a military escalation.
title: Border crisis exposes Cambodia’s murky political economy

summary: A three-day meeting of the Regional Border Committee (RBC) secretariat held at the Poipet-Aranyaprathet border crossing ended on January 29 without a consensus. Military officials from Cambodia's 5th Military Region and Thailand's 1st Army Area, observed by the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT), agreed to continue exchanging documents and negotiating from their respective headquarters. This follows the December 27 ceasefire after weeks of armed conflict.
title: Cambodia - Thailand meeting over border issues ends with no consensus

summary: Foreign ministers from Southeast Asia met in Cebu, Philippines, for an informal retreat to discuss regional security, including the ongoing Thailand-Cambodia border conflict. Philippine Foreign Minister Ma. Theresa Lazaro emphasized the need for a rules-based approach and restraint. The conflict remains a top priority alongside the Myanmar crisis and South China Sea tensions as the Philippines takes the ASEAN chair for 2026.
title: Philippines hosts ASEAN foreign minister retreat to tackle regional issues

summary: During an ASEAN foreign ministers' retreat in Cebu, Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro highlighted the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict as a significant challenge to regional stability. The meeting addressed the 'deadly fighting' that occurred before the US-backed ceasefire in late 2025. Lazaro urged member states to maintain restraint and adhere to international law to preserve peace in the face of growing geopolitical tensions and unilateral actions.
title: ASEAN should adhere to rule of law in face of 'unilateral actions,' Philippines' top diplomat says

summary: A three-day meeting of the Regional Border Committee (RBC) secretariat between Cambodia's 5th Military Region and Thailand's 1st Army Area concluded on Thursday without reaching a consensus. Held at the Poipet-Sa Kaeo border under ASEAN observation, the talks aimed to address ongoing border issues following the December 27 ceasefire. Both sides agreed to continue exchanging documents and negotiating from their respective headquarters.
title: Cambodia-Thailand RBC secretariat meeting over border issues concludes with no consensus

summary: Lt Gen Kanok Netrawatthanasena reported significant defensive preparations, including trenches and bunkers, at disputed border areas like Ta Muen Thom Temple. He argued these movements indicate both sides are positioning for another clash, despite the official ceasefire.
title: Thai ex-deputy commander warns third round of fighting ‘will happen’

summary: The Thai military's Joint Information Centre addressed Cambodian allegations of ceasefire violations between Jan 12-22, 2026. Thailand clarified that its use of drones, installation of temporary barriers, and demining activities were routine security measures within its designated deployment areas and did not violate sovereignty. The statement reaffirmed respect for the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) monitoring the border.
title: Thai military responds to Cambodia’s ceasefire violation claims, reaffirms commitment to GBC guidelines

summary: Two days of military-level talks in Poipet between Thailand’s First Army Region and Cambodia’s 5th Regional Army ended without an agreement. The dispute focuses on the management of border areas in Sa Kaeo province, specifically Ban Nong Chan and Ban Ta Kuan, which saw heavy fighting in December. No new date has been set for future meetings.
title: Talks between Thai and Cambodian armies end in deadlock
